core_claim: The explanation is generated from the same V4 inference computation used to produce the displayed prediction.

input_contract.preprocessing: The explainer consumes the ALREADY-SCALED inference tensor. It implements no second preprocessing path: dataset explanations read the pre-built multiday_benchmark_K5 .npy arrays; PCAP explanations reuse src/pcap_ingest_v4.py's build_sequences() output verbatim.

TARGET_A_horizon_probability.definition: P(attack at t+5) = sigmoid(attack_head(z_5)), z_5 = transition_step^5(encode(x)); identical to k_step_rollout(x, K).probs[5]
TARGET_A_horizon_probability.threshold_provenance: validation-selected, frozen in docs/v4_baseline_manifest.json; never re-selected here

TARGET_B_trajectory_max.definition: MAX is non-differentiable at ties. The explainer attributes the fixed horizon k* = argmax at the input, so the attributed function value equals the displayed max exactly. In 43.8% of sampled windows the argmax changes somewhere along the straight-line integration path, so the completeness reference is F_k*(baseline), not max(baseline). Recorded per sample in trajectory_max_explanations.csv.

attribution_method.n_steps_rationale: chosen from the measured convergence sweep in completeness_checks.csv (50/128/256/1024); 1024 is the first setting with worst-case mean relative completeness error below 1% at every evaluated horizon. Not chosen for appearance.

rejected_methods.attention: V4 has no attention mechanism; no attention-based explanation is produced and no attribution is called 'attention'
rejected_methods.shap: src/shap_explainer.py is retained for the historical V3 artifacts only; it is not provenance-locked, targets a single transition step, reads temporal_benchmark_v2, and draws a random baseline without a seed

attribution_method.gradients: enabled through the input; parameters never updated

baseline_definition.primary: zero vector in scaled feature space, shape (10, 52)
baseline_definition.rationale: The frozen StandardScaler subtracts the training-partition mean, so the zero vector IS the average training window held constant across all 10 history windows. It is label-free, uses no test data, and is exactly reproducible.
baseline_definition.secondary_sensitivity_baseline: mean of the 6568 fully-benign TRAINING sequences (A_binary_multistep_train all-zero); training labels only, never test labels
baseline_definition.caveat: A constant-over-time reference window is not itself a realisable capture. This is the standard IG reference-point compromise and is reported, not hidden.

representative_case_policy.label: A_binary_multistep_test[:, 4]  (attack present at t+5)
representative_case_policy.high_confidence: argmax p over all test sequences
representative_case_policy.low_confidence: argmin p over all test sequences
representative_case_policy.median_rule: sort the group's probabilities ascending, take element n//2; ties broken by ascending sample index
representative_case_policy.not_selected_on: explanation content, attribution magnitude, or agreement with any expected narrative

randomization_test.acceptance_rule: mean |spearman| of SIGNED attribution between the real and randomised models below 0.30, averaged over three seeds -- learned structure must be lost

perturbation_test.acceptance_rule: mean |dP| for top-attributed features must exceed that of the low-attribution control

completeness_test.acceptance_rule: PRIMARY: the attributed output is a probability in [0, 1], so the completeness residual |sum(attr) - (F(x) - F(baseline))| is read on the probability scale -- mean AND p99 absolute error must be below 0.01 (one probability point) at every evaluated horizon. SECONDARY: mean relative error below 1% restricted to the well-posed subset |F(x) - F(baseline)| > 0.05.

mitre_separation.rule: Attribution never produces ATT&CK labels. The MITRE layer (src/mitre_mapper.py) is rule-based over feature VALUES and runs independently of attribution values. Any joint display must label the two blocks separately: 'MODEL ATTRIBUTION' and 'ATT&CK INTERPRETATION (rule-based)'.

pcap_policy.required_caveat: The PCAP explanation uses the same V4 feature contract and transform chain, but flow-record production differences can affect the resulting values. Task 7 proved exact parity for the 26 base-feature aggregations, the 26 relative-change features, all transforms, the scaler interface and 10-second windowing; flow-record production remains APPROXIMATE. These values are NOT numerically equivalent to training features.

limitations: Attribution measures model sensitivity/contribution. It does NOT establish causality, attacker intent, attack stage, actual compromise, or root cause.
Integrated Gradients is a path-integral approximation; the residual completeness error is reported per sample in completeness_checks.csv and is not zero.
Attributions are baseline-relative. A different reference point yields different values; the baseline-sensitivity overlap is recorded in completeness_checks.csv.
The trajectory-max target is attributed at a fixed argmax; in 43.8% of sampled windows the argmax changes along the integration path.
PCAP explanations inherit the Task 7 finding: flow-record production is APPROXIMATE, so PCAP feature values are not numerically equivalent to training features.

The V4 checkpoint was trained on single-day temporal_benchmark_v2 arrays and evaluated on multiday_benchmark_K5 arrays scaled by a different StandardScaler (frozen-baseline known issue). Explanations inherit that out-of-distribution-normalisation regime.
Re-batching the same frozen model shifts LSTM reduction order by up to 1.5e-06; identity is therefore asserted on the identical tensor in the identical batch.
No K=4 reference threshold exists, so K=4 is not explained against a frozen threshold.
